answer: To earn access to an agent economy, each new identity must lock a scarce token in a public, time-locked bond, then complete tasks whose results are checked by randomly assigned, bonded peers. A trellis of repeat interactions lets the system weight proven reliability, while an orchard of fresh identities starts with little influence. If peers catch fabricated work, the bond is slashed; creating a spiral of disposable accounts therefore requires tying up real capital and risking its loss for every identity.
